title: Bound score-level artifact fanout in living reports
description:
As an optimization operator, I want milestone publication to create individual score briefs only for scores with stakeholder-relevant detail, so that the living Report becomes useful promptly without losing complete portfolio and scorecard evidence.

Feature: Bound score-level artifact fanout

Scenario: Ranking publishes a bounded actionable artifact set
  Given a complete portfolio containing many scores
  And only a subset appears in priorities, questions, issues, or optimization outcomes
  When the ranking milestone is published
  Then every score remains in the stakeholder workbook and scorecard-level CSV
  And an individual Markdown score brief is published only for that stakeholder-relevant subset
  And the published artifact plan exactly reconciles with the uploaded artifacts

Scenario: A later finding creates a score brief
  Given a score did not require an individual brief in an earlier milestone
  When a later milestone adds that score to a stakeholder question or optimization outcome
  Then that milestone publishes a score brief for the score
  And the scorecard presentation links to the exact immutable brief revision

Scenario: Unchanged relevant briefs are reused
  Given a stakeholder-relevant score brief was committed in the prior milestone
  When the next milestone leaves its content unchanged
  Then the prior verified artifact is reused
  And no duplicate upload is required

Out of scope:
- Removing any score from the portfolio workbook or scorecard CSV.
- Weakening checksum, reconciliation, privacy, or fatal-publication guarantees.
- Parallel or unordered artifact writes.
- Automatic score, guideline, champion, or feedback-setting mutation.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text:
Production-backed dogfood evidence exposed an account-wide ranking publication bottleneck: 1,262 artifacts were planned before assessment could begin, including 1,105 individual score briefs. The durable ranking revision remained unavailable while the live status advanced through the uploads. At 997/1,262, publication had consumed about 494 seconds.

Inversion decision: do not trade away atomic publication, checksums, privacy, immutable evidence, interruption recovery, or fatal failure semantics. Bound only score-level Markdown fanout. Keep every portfolio row in the workbook and every scorecard summary/CSV/presentation; create individual briefs only for scores represented in priorities, stakeholder questions/issues, or optimization outcomes.

A Terra Coding Agent added failing outside-in specifications, implemented the shared selector, and returned 90 passing report tests. Direct Product Owner/Engineering Lead review found an opaque-ID mismatch in issue lookup; the agent corrected it and added duplicate-name regression coverage. Main-agent validation currently passes 90 run-report tests and 142 portfolio-run tests. The live baseline run continues under the pre-fix loaded code so its timing remains honest.
